clue.text: Run across a little irritation

indicators.note: across signals that the word for run stretches over the other pieces, holding them inside

parts.note: to run away is to flee
a little is a bit

explanation.surface: Someone stumbles on a minor annoyance in passing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'across' makes the escape word straddle the rest; 'Run' is flight, not a jog or a ladder in tights.
explanation.definitionFit: A bite from a flea is the classic trivial annoyance, hence any small nuisance.

clue.text: With pleasure, clasp pen

definitions.meaning: to embrace someone warmly, as in gathering a loved one into one's arms

explanation.walkthrough: One sense is the verb used of hugging someone to your bosom; the other is the sheep enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheep enclosure is a fold, and to fold someone in your arms is to hug them gladly.

clue.text: Bad feeling when messenger drops round

indicators.note: drops means the messenger lets go of one piece, so it is taken out

parts.note: an envoy is a diplomatic messenger
a round thing is shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A courier loses a lap and resentment follows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drops' removes O from ENVOY.
explanation.definitionFit: Resentful jealousy of another's good fortune is an unpleasant emotion.

clue.text: Moses was discovered in these papyri

definitions.meaning: in the Bible the infant Moses was found hidden among reeds by the Nile
papyrus plants are tall reeds growing in marshes

explanation.walkthrough: The King James Bible says Moses' basket was laid in the flags; tradition calls the reeds bulrushes.
explanation.definitionFit: Papyrus is a type of tall marsh reed, the plant called the bulrush in the Moses story.

clue.text: Subtle comedy, having to cure cold in the autumn weather

indicators.note: in places the cure and the cold inside the word the

parts.note: to cure is to heal
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
Keats's season of mists: mist is typical autumn weather

explanation.surface: A gentle comedy about getting over a chill in foggy autumn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the container. Subtle is the con-man alchemist in Ben Jonson's 1610 comedy, so 'Subtle comedy' reads as an adjective but names the play by its hero.
explanation.definitionFit: Ben Jonson's comedy features the trickster Subtle, so it is the play in which he appears.

clue.text: Fish hook takes eel, oddly

parts.note: a barb is a hook, or the backward point on one

indicators.note: oddly means take the odd-numbered letters of the word eel

explanation.surface: An angler's hook catches an eel in a strange way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes the first and third letters of eel, E and L.
explanation.definitionFit: A barbel is a freshwater fish of the carp family with whiskers round its mouth.

clue.text: President Hoover, for one, found in a second

indicators.note: found in says the barrier is placed inside the other pieces

parts.note: the Hoover Dam on the Colorado River is a dam

explanation.surface: Herbert Hoover turns up in a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: Hoover looks like the president, but it is the Hoover Dam. 'found in' puts DAM inside A and S.
explanation.definitionFit: John Adams and John Quincy Adams were both US presidents.

clue.text: Caesar's last word, warning about constant violence

parts.note: Shakespeare's Caesar dies saying Et tu, Brute

indicators.note: about means the warning cry goes round the constant

parts.note: fore is the golfer's warning shout
C is the symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light

explanation.surface: Caesar's dying words amount to a caution against continual violence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts C inside FORE.
explanation.definitionFit: Brute force is crude physical violence rather than subtlety.

clue.text: Just out of it, Hollywood fails to retain financial supporter

indicators.note: to retain means the word for fails holds the backer inside

parts.note: to lose is to fail
an angel is a financial backer of a theatrical show

explanation.surface: A film capital fails to keep its investor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to retain' puts ANGEL inside LOSES. Hollywood stands for the city it is part of.
explanation.definitionFit: Hollywood is a district of the Californian city and the byword for it as film capital.

clue.text: Good lookers find only half an amaranth

indicators.note: only half means keep just the first half of the plant name

parts.note: ...-bleeding is a species of amaranth with drooping red flowers

explanation.surface: Attractive people discover just part of a flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'only half' keeps the first eight letters of LOVE-LIES-BLEEDING.
explanation.definitionFit: Lovelies is a colloquial plural noun for beautiful people, especially women.

clue.text: Resistance? It's spurned by aristocrat

indicators.note: spurned by means the aristocrat rejects a letter, which is taken out

parts.note: a marquis is a nobleman ranking between duke and earl
it refers back to resistance, whose symbol is R in physics

explanation.surface: Resistance is rejected by the nobility.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spurned by' removes R from MARQUIS. 'It' points back to Resistance, abbreviated R.
explanation.definitionFit: The Maquis was the French Resistance in rural areas during the Second World War.

clue.text: Sort of killer, more unfeeling, that may Check tod be seen on your TV

parts.note: a serial killer is one type of murderer
number means more numb, more lacking feeling

explanation.surface: A murderer, ever colder, turns up on your television screen.
explanation.walkthrough: NUMBER is NUMB with -ER, more numb, not the counting word. 'Check tod' is stray text in the clue as held, and 'that may be' joins the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A serial number is printed on appliances such as a television set for identification.

clue.text: Indulge ridiculously unbending courtier

indicators.note: ridiculously means the letters of indulge are rearranged absurdly

parts.note: unbending means stern, unyielding

explanation.surface: A strict courtier spoils himself absurdly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ridiculously' turns INDULGE into GUILDEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Guildenstern is a courtier in Hamlet, partnered with Rosencrantz.

clue.text: Before voyeur, slip is changed

indicators.note: is changed means the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Before the peeping tom, a mistake gets corrected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is changed' rearranges VOYEURSLIP.
explanation.definitionFit: Previously means earlier, at a prior time, so it can stand for before as an adverb.

clue.text: Lungs exercised by idiots? These offer a sight more protection

definitions.text: These offer a sight more protection

indicators.note: exercised means the letters of lungs are worked about

parts.note: asses are fools

explanation.surface: Fools give their lungs a workout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exercised' turns LUNGS into SUNGL. 'a sight more' plays on 'a lot more' and on eyesight.
explanation.definitionFit: Dark glasses shield the eyes, giving the organs of sight more protection from glare.

clue.text: Cosmetic is pointless: hard and scratchy

indicators.note: is pointless means a compass point, E for east, is removed

parts.note: rouge is a red make-up for the cheeks
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Make-up is useless, and it feels harsh on the skin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is pointless' removes E (east, a compass point) from ROUGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough surface is coarse and abrasive, so it feels scratchy to the touch.

clue.text: Welcomes shade, though it's a bit icy

parts.note: to hail someone is to greet or welcome them
a shade of colour is a tone

explanation.surface: Someone greets the shade, although the weather is a bit chilly.
explanation.definitionFit: A pellet of ice falling from a storm cloud is a small piece of ice.

clue.text: City authority absorbs almost all of NI town

indicators.note: absorbs means the word for authority takes the town inside it

parts.note: having the say is having authority

indicators.note: almost all of means the last letter of the town is dropped

parts.note: Lisburn is a city in Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A local authority swallows most of a Northern Irish town.
explanation.walkthrough: NI is Northern Ireland; 'almost all of' cuts the town's final N, and 'absorbs' wraps the result. Salisbury is the Wiltshire cathedral city.
explanation.definitionFit: Salisbury is a cathedral city in Wiltshire, England.

clue.text: Gives out sorted mail — all on base score

indicators.note: out means the letters of gives are disordered
sorted means the letters of mail are rearranged, as at a sorting office

explanation.surface: A postman hands out sorted letters, all of them to the base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' turns GIVES into VIGES and 'sorted' turns MAIL into IMAL. A score is twenty.
explanation.definitionFit: Vigesimal counting works in twenties, a score being twenty, so it is based on that number.

clue.text: Temptation to conceal clubs' profits

indicators.note: to conceal means the temptation hides the clubs inside it

parts.note: a lure is an enticement
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

explanation.surface: Lure is used to hide a club's earnings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to conceal' puts C inside LURE.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucre is money or gain, usually with a sense of greed, as in filthy lucre.

clue.text: Old testing-grounds void — concentrate!

parts.note: ranges are areas for testing weapons
to quash a verdict is to void it

explanation.surface: Old test sites are declared invalid, so pay attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concentrate' reads as an order to focus, but it is a noun: a diluted drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Orange squash is a concentrated fruit cordial diluted with water before drinking.

clue.text: Collect harvest, involving ears, in the country

annotationWithheld.why: Collect harvest, involving ears, in the country (5) for GHANA: no parse of the wordplay gives GHANA; a word looks misread
annotationWithheld.clue: Collect harvest, involving ears, in the country

clue.text: Stringed instrument without one virtuoso

indicators.note: without means the instrument loses one letter

parts.note: the sitar is an Indian stringed instrument
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A virtuoso plays a stringed instrument missing a part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes I from SITAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A star is an outstandingly talented performer, as a virtuoso is.

clue.text: Short mixed contest for boat

indicators.note: short means the event name is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: a pro-am is a golf tournament mixing professionals and amateurs

explanation.surface: A brief mixed tournament for boats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' removes M from PROAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A proa is a Malay or Pacific sailing vessel with an outrigger.

clue.text: Band always parade

parts.note: a sash is a band of cloth worn over the shoulder
ay, also spelt aye, is an old word for ever or always

explanation.surface: A band is always on parade.
explanation.definitionFit: To sashay is to walk showily, so it means to parade or flounce along.

clue.text: Muscle used by kidnapper

definitions.meaning: a muscle that draws a limb away from the body's midline
one who carries a person off by force

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses come from Latin abducere, to lead away: a limb or a person.

clue.text: No supporter of independence

parts.note: read as a political voter, it seems a unionist; really a person who never says no, with no independent mind

explanation.definitionFit: A sycophant who always agrees with superiors shows no independence of thought.

clue.text: Retirement village for which responsibility is unclear

definitions.meaning: jokingly, a district full of grey-haired old people
a situation not clearly covered by existing rules

explanation.definitionFit: An ill-defined zone between categories, whose ownership or rules are uncertain, is an ambiguous situation.
